2. `keydown(Enter)` → `finishEditing()` → `destroyTodo()` → `render()` → orphan re-attached (because `editingId` still matches) then removed again

The re-attachment during the second `render()` is the defect. The `parentNode` guard catches it in the simple case, but the re-entrant blur timing in a real browser creates the `removeChild` error.

**Fix指引:** Add `editingId = null;` in `destroyTodo()` when the destroyed todo is the one being edited.

**Acceptance test:** `should respect the back button`
**Spec:** `features/browser-acceptance-defects.feature:66`

1. Remove `e.preventDefault()` from the filter click handler and let the default anchor behaviour update the hash (the existing `hashchange` listener will call `handleHashChange()` → `setFilter()`)

Feature: Browser acceptance defects
  As a user interacting with the app in a real browser
  I want the app to handle real browser event sequences correctly
  So that editing-to-empty and back-button routing work without errors

  Background:
    Given the app is loaded

  # ── Defect 1: Editing to empty via blur + Enter ────────────────────────
  # In a real browser, pressing Enter on an empty edit input fires both
  # a keydown(Enter) event and a blur event (because the input loses
  # focus during DOM manipulation).  Both handlers call finishEditing()
  # → destroyTodo() → render().  The first render()'s orphan-removal
  # loop calls parentNode.removeChild(li), which detaches the input,
  # firing blur synchronously mid-loop.  The blur handler re-enters
  # render(), removing the same orphan.  The original loop then tries
  # removeChild on a node whose parentNode no longer considers it a
  # child, throwing: "Failed to execute 'removeChild' on 'Node'".
  #
  # The in-harness suite dispatches only one event at a time, so the
  # re-entrant render never occurs and the scenario passes.

  Rule: Editing to empty must not throw when both blur and Enter fire

    Scenario: Clearing edit input via simultaneous blur and Enter destroys the todo without error
      Given a todo "Buy milk" exists
      When the user double-clicks the label of todo "Buy milk"
      And the user clears the edit input and fires blur and Enter together
      Then the todo "Buy milk" no longer exists
      And the todo list is empty

    Scenario: Destroying an editing todo clears the editing state
      Given a todo "Buy milk" exists
      When the user double-clicks the label of todo "Buy milk"
      And the user clears the edit input and fires blur and Enter together
      Then no todo is in editing mode

  @contract
  Scenario: Render guards orphan removal against detached nodes
    Given the app source is loaded
    Then the render function contains a parentNode guard in the orphan-removal loop

  @contract
  Scenario: Destroying a todo clears editing state to prevent re-attachment during re-entrant render
    Given the app source is loaded
    Then the destroyTodo function clears the editingId variable

  # ── Defect 2: Routing — back button after filter clicks ────────────────
  # The filter click handler calls e.preventDefault() but never updates
  # window.location.hash.  So clicking filter links does not push
  # history entries.  When the user presses the browser back button,
  # history.back() has nothing to go back to — the hash stays the same,
  # hashchange never fires, and the filter does not change.
  #
  # The in-harness suite manually sets the hash via navigate() which
  # always pushes a history entry, masking the defect.  In a real
  # browser, clicking a filter link should update the hash so that
  # history.back() restores the previous filter.

  Rule: Filter links must update the URL hash so back button works

    Scenario: Clicking a filter link updates the hash
      Given a todo "Buy milk" exists
      When the user clicks the "Active" filter link
      Then the window hash is "#/active"

    Scenario: Clicking the All filter link updates the hash
      Given the following todos exist:
